outcome_measure: Shortest accepted time-to-contact (TTC, s) of the approaching vehicle at the moment of stepping back (lower = riskier crossing)
comparison: Real street: pedestrians with auditory perception vs pedestrians wearing hearing protection (no vehicle sound)
values_verbatim: "The results revealed a significant main effect of the sound condition in both the real environment, F(1, 28) = 4.25, p = .049"; "In the real environment, participants without sound exhibited an average TTC value that was 0.30 s shorter than those with sound"; real environment TTC with sound M = 2.9 s, SD = 1.2; real environment TTC without sound M = 2.6 s, SD = 0.9
n_info: 15 participants with sound and 15 without sound (between-subjects); 15 repetitions each, 450 real-street trials in total; the reported SDs accompany group-level TTC means in §4.3 and it is not stated whether they are computed over participants or over trials
quote: "In the real environment, participants without sound exhibited an average TTC value that was 0.30 s shorter than those with sound."
